data.sourceWord: MCQ: Means of salvation in Christianity
data.targetWord: Grace — the free, unmerited favour of God that enables salvation. Christians believe God's grace, shown supremely through Christ's death and resurrection, saves humans from sin regardless of their own merit.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.1 (1 mark) — Answer: B Grace

data.targetWord: Christians believe heaven is where God dwells, a place of perfect goodness, peace and joy where there is no pain or suffering. Souls enter heaven when their sins are forgiven, as a reward for following Christian teaching.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — Give two Christian beliefs about heaven

data.targetWord: Heaven offers the opportunity to be reunited with family and friends in an eternal, spiritual state of being. Many Christians picture it as being in the presence of God on a throne, with angels present, opposite to hell.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — Give two Christian beliefs about heaven

data.targetWord: Belief in the Oneness of God means Christians direct all worship exclusively to God, building a personal relationship through prayer and pilgrimage. Because there is only one God, he receives their full faith and devotion, influencing daily acts of worship.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.3 (4 marks) — Explain two ways belief in the Oneness of God influences Christians today

data.sourceWord: Influence of monotheism — Trinity and mission
data.targetWord: Monotheism strengthens belief in the Trinity as three aspects of one God (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), encouraging Christians to include all three in worship. It may also motivate evangelism — believing one God is supreme may lead Christians to share their faith with others.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.3 (4 marks) — Explain two ways belief in the Oneness of God influences Christians today

data.targetWord: Jesus' crucifixion atoned for the original sin of Adam and Eve, removing the barrier between humanity and God caused by sin. Christians believe that through Jesus' sacrifice they can receive forgiveness and eternal life if they repent and have faith.

examples.en-GB: 'For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.' (Romans 6:23)

data.targetWord: By experiencing pain and suffering on the cross, Jesus enables Christians to accept suffering in their own lives, knowing he understood and shared human experience. His suffering shows that death is not the end and made the resurrection possible.

examples.en-GB: 'Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one's life for one's friends.' (John 15:13)

data.targetWord: 'He is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.' (1 John 2:2) — This shows the universal scope of Christ's saving work through the crucifixion.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.4 (5 marks) — scripture reference for the Crucifixion

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love shown through Creation
data.targetWord: God created the world and all living creatures out of love, demonstrating his benevolent nature. Christians believe that creation itself is an expression of God's love, and he wants the best for everything he made. This gives strong grounds for believing God is always loving.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.5 (12 marks) — Evaluate: 'For Christians, it is right to believe that God is always loving'

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love shown through the Incarnation
data.targetWord: God's most loving act was sending his Son to die for humanity's sins, opening the way to eternal life. 'God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.' (John 3:16) — this supreme sacrifice demonstrates unconditional love.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.5 (12 marks) — Evaluate: 'For Christians, it is right to believe that God is always loving'

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love extends to all through forgiveness
data.targetWord: God's perfect love extends to all who faithfully ask for forgiveness, regardless of what they have done. No one is excluded from the possibility of God's love. Christians are commanded to love enemies as God loves all, showing his love is universal and unconditional.

examples.en-GB: 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your Father in heaven.' (Matthew 5:44)

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Problem of evil challenges God's love
data.targetWord: The existence of suffering and evil in the world is difficult to reconcile with belief in a God who is always loving. If God were truly all-loving, he would prevent unnecessary suffering, yet natural disasters and disease continue — suggesting God either cannot or does not always act out of love.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.5 (12 marks) — Arguments against 'God is always loving'

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Old Testament portrays God as wrathful
data.targetWord: In the Old Testament, God does not always appear all-loving — the drowning of the Egyptian army during the Exodus and the destruction of Jericho suggest a wrathful, judgemental God. These acts challenge the idea that God is consistently and always loving throughout scripture.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.5 (12 marks) — Arguments against 'God is always loving'

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: God's love is beyond human comprehension
data.targetWord: Although Christians believe God is the sum of all perfections, being 'always loving' may be impossible for humans to fully comprehend. Applying human concepts of love to an infinite God may be misleading — what appears unloving from a human perspective may serve a higher divine purpose we cannot understand.
